title: PRIMUS, a wheel-legged biped
summary: A self-balancing robot with closed five-bar legs that I designed in Fusion 360 and built. Its CAD becomes a MuJoCo model, a model-based controller balances it, and learned policies add robustness and hops over steps and gaps.
lead: PRIMUS balances on two wheels and uses its legs as active suspension. This page follows it from the CAD to the controller, the learned skills and the pilot interface, with an interactive model of every part.

media.alt: PRIMUS rendered in Blender from the CAD: a dark grey body on two aluminium five-bar legs ending in black wheels.
media.thumbnailAlt: The PRIMUS robot rendered from its CAD model

title: Building PRIMUS
summary: An animated, step-by-step build of the PRIMUS wheel-legged biped generated from its Fusion 360 assembly: the actuators part by part, the hip modules, body, legs and covers, with the bill of materials.
lead: Thirty-four steps from loose parts to a standing robot, starting inside the actuators. Each step plays as a 3D animation built from the CAD: parts come in from where you would bring them, screws turn in under a hex key and inserts go in under the iron.

media.alt: PRIMUS fully assembled, rendered in Blender from the CAD: dark grey printed body, aluminium legs and green actuator housings on two black wheels.

title: PRIMUS: control and reinforcement learning
summary: How PRIMUS balances and learns: the half-robot model and its equations, the gain-scheduled LQR, virtual model control through the five-bar, and the residual and skill reinforcement-learning experiments in MuJoCo Warp.
lead: The physics, the model-based controller with its math, and what the reinforcement-learning experiments taught, from the first failed run to the current skill policy.

title: Structure-aware DJ transitions
summary: A browser-based DJ assistant trained on song structure. It maps verses and choruses, recommends the next track and cue points, and mixes the handoff live.
lead: Our DJ assistant can leave one song at the end of a chorus and enter the next at the start of a verse. A CNN and bidirectional LSTM map the arrangement of each track. Claude uses those maps to recommend a transition the DJ can hear and adjust in the browser.

media.alt: Two translucent records in turquoise and pink with yellow cue markers, an illustration of a handoff between tracks.
media.thumbnailAlt: Two color-coded records marked for a transition
media.caption: Example transition plan. A low-pass sweep connects the outgoing chorus to the incoming track.

title: NightCurve: optimizing a trajectory under uncertainty
summary: A constrained trajectory optimization project. A Swift solver integrates a nonlinear model, searches over discrete events and continuous timing, and tests the finalists under parameter uncertainty.
lead: I built NightCurve to study constrained trajectory tracking. The input is a hand-drawn blood alcohol concentration (BAC) curve. The unknowns are the events that might reproduce it in a nonlinear simulation. In this seven-hour example the simulated median peaks an hour and a half early. The objective function explains why a schedule can miss that landmark and still win.

media.alt: A seven-hour target, simulated median and percentile band for a synthetic NightCurve run.
media.thumbnailAlt: NightCurve app icon with a glowing curve above a night skyline
